teams.heading: Fiji pitch pride over money in bid to lure Mark Nawaqanitawase
teams.body: Fiji are pitching pride over money in their bid to lure Mark Nawaqanitawase. The pursuit has become public: Fiji have broken their silence on his possible defection, while the player has spoken about a decision he says people will never understand. It is a live question for a side that, after Jake White named his first squad, is still building its identity.

lead.why: It is a new, live Fiji story about a player the squad is trying to keep, and it is not a repeat of the White squad, Gatland or coaching-identity items already run.

teams.heading: Jack van Poortvliet signs multi-year Leicester deal, eyeing England's 2027 World Cup
teams.body: England scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet has signed a new multi-year deal with Leicester Tigers. The 25-year-old has made 118 first-team appearances since graduating in 2019, and he already holds an England contract for 2026-27. Van Poortvliet, who has 27 England caps, missed the 2023 World Cup after an ankle injury in a warm-up game, and he will hope to play a big role in England's 2027 World Cup campaign in Australia. "It was a pretty easy decision to stay," he told the club website.

lead.why: A new item on a current England squad player's contract, and the only fresh men's England story in the shortlist; the top item is analysis of the squad already reported today.

teams.heading: Jeremy Ward, South African-born, named in France's 42-player Nations Championship squad
teams.body: France have confirmed South African-born centre Jeremy Ward in their 42-player squad for the Nations Championship, the call-up flagged by SA Rugby Magazine. Named by Fabien Galthié on Wednesday, Ward is a Stade Français teammate of Tani Vili, and the squad is built to fill gaps left by injury. The catch: he will not be eligible to play for France until next year, just before the World Cup in Australia, so this is a squad place for now.

The next of those Tests is against Argentina.

teams.heading: Italy's last five: one win and four defeats, latest 57-10 to Australia
teams.body: In their last five games Italy have won one and lost four, most recent first: loss, loss, loss, loss, win. The current run stands at four straight defeats, and the latest was a 57-10 loss away to Australia in July's Nations Championship group stage. The next fixture on the calendar is a meeting with South Africa.

teams.heading: Tom English tips Freddy Douglas and Ollie Blyth-Lafferty for Scotland call-ups
teams.body: BBC Sport's Tom English reckons Ollie Blyth-Lafferty, 20, must have a big chance at tighthead for next month's Nations Championship. Freddy Douglas, who started against Fiji in the summer and played roughly the last dozen minutes of the Six Nations win over France, is blocked at seven by Rory Darge's consistency. English sees him scrapping for a bench place and also flags Seb Stephen, 21, as one of the few young players in the mix.

teams.heading: Ebbw Vale's Curtis Gregory sent off for stamp; WRU awaits referee's report
teams.body: Ebbw Vale's Curtis Gregory was shown a straight red card for stamping on an opponent in Thursday night's Super Rygbi Cymru club match against Llandovery, a game shown live on S4C. Referee Craig Evans issued a permanent red in the 35th minute, and footage of the incident has been picked up by news outlets in South Africa and Australia. The Welsh Rugby Union is awaiting the official's report before a disciplinary panel considers sanctions, and calls for a lifetime ban are growing.

lead.why: The strongest new item in today's pack; the Wales v Japan preview is already run and no new men's national-team story broke.

teams.heading: Contepomi brings back captain Montoya and Kremer for 33-man training camp
teams.body: Felipe Contepomi has recalled captain Julián Montoya and enforcer Marcos Kremer for a 33-man squad that assembles from Monday for a three-day camp, his strongest roster of the year according to Americas Rugby News. Montoya and Kremer both missed the recent home tests against Australia and South Africa. Ignacio Ruiz and Joaquín Oviedo are injured, and Benjamín Grondona and Matías Moroni are not included. Contepomi confirms his November squad after the camp, and the end-of-year tour takes in Ireland, Italy and France.

lead.why: It is Argentina's own squad news, and the pack covers it directly, so it beats the Prendergast thread, which concerns an Irish player.

teams.heading: Miles Amatosero earns Wallabies recall despite red card and suspension history
teams.body: Waratahs brawler Miles Amatosero earns a recall to the Wallabies squad despite a shaky disciplinary record, back from injury for the Northern Hemisphere tour. He was banned at the start of the season for punching clubmate Angus Scott-Young in training, and his second cap, off the bench against Japan, ended in a red card and a three-match suspension after a clash with captain Warner Dearns. Kiss has picked him anyway, naming him in the 33-man group for the tour.

teams.heading: Warner Deans returns from injury as Japan face Fiji without Michael Leitch
teams.body: Warner Deans is back from injury for Japan's JRFU 100th Anniversary Match against Fiji today, after training camps brought his return alongside props Yota Kamimori and Keijiro Tamesawa and backs Shinya Komura and Yoshihei Ishida. Michael Leitch is still absent, stuck on 97 caps. Charlie Lawrence and Koga Nezuka are called up for the first time this year. Fiji, under new coach Jake White, name four uncapped players among their starters and reserves. Japan won the Pacific Nations Cup final against them in September, their first title since 2019.

teams.heading: Steve Hansen labels World Rugby a 'secret society' before November referee summit
teams.body: Former All Blacks coach Sir Steve Hansen has accused World Rugby of being a 'secret society', claiming it has not told anyone about a directive to referees on the TMO. On the Rugby Unity podcast he said the yellow card needs urgent work, pointing to too many matches where sides play a man down, 13 on 15 or 14 on 15, for unintentional offences. With a World Rugby summit of coaches and referees due in November, when New Zealand's Scotland Test falls, Hansen wants the conversation to be open.

lead.why: The only shortlist item that is not already in this tab's recent editions, and it bears on New Zealand's November Tests.

teams.heading: Springboks' Andre Esterhuizen hobbles off with foot injury after 52 seconds
teams.body: Rassie Erasmus has a concern after Sharks captain Andre Esterhuizen was forced off inside the first minute of Friday's United Rugby Championship match. The inside centre landed awkwardly on his right foot after an aerial contest and could not stand on it, with Jaco Williams coming on. Erasmus is expected to name his Nations Championship squad in the coming week, and Esterhuizen has been a vital cog recently, switching between backline and forwards.

lead.why: A new injury to a Springboks centre ahead of the Nations Championship squad announcement is the story a fan would text a mate about.
